newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO View - Hot response seen for Beijing Enterprises.
newsitem.headline: IPO View - Hot response seen for Beijing Enterprises.

text.p: Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, should receive a strong response at its initial public offering (IPO) scheduled to take place in Hong Kong this week, analysts said.
The Beijing municipal government-backed conglomerate's interests include manufacturing, retailing, road operations, telecommunications, and property investment.

"The response is expected to be strong because of its assets injection concept," said Manus Tam, corporate finance director at Lippo Securities, referring to possible future purchases of assets by Beijing Enterprises from its parent.
The company's close links with its Beijing parent should also give it access to high quality projects, analysts said.
Beijing Enterprises is the primary commercial vehicle for the Beijing municipal government to gain access to capital, technology and management expertise in international markets.
The company is one of the so-called "red-chip window" companies established in Hong Kong by Chinese authorities as a bridge to the outside commercial world.
Beijing Enterprises' IPO is expected to run from May 20 to 23 with dealing in shares due to begin on May 29, analysts said.
"Everything is built on the red-chip fancy," said Lan Xue, associate director of SocGen-Crosby Securities, referring to the current popularity of shares of China-backed companies.
She said Shanghai Industrial was set to become the most successful story of the red chip companies, adding: "Many people are branding Beijing Enterprises as the next Shanghai Industrial."

The share price of Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, a Shanghai municipal government-backed company, has leapt more than five times from its issue price of HK$7.28 within 12 months of its listing last May.
Beijing Enterprises expects to issue 150 million shares of which 10 percent is expected to be offered to the Hong Kong public and 90 percent designated for international placement.

The company had originally planned to price the shares at HK$8 to HK$9.70 per share, but last week decided to raise the offering price range to HK$11.50 to HK$12.50 because of strong interest, analysts said.
"It may scale down a little bit ... (depending on) how many people are going to subscribe to the IPO, but I don't really think it is too serious," Xue said.
The new issue price will represent a price/earnings multiple (P/E) of 17.95 to 19.35 times, up from the initial 12.7 to 14.8 times, they said.

Pamela Lam, analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities, said: "Even though the P/E has been raised to about 19 times, the stock is relatively cheap compared with a P/E average of about 30 to 40 times for other red chips."
Lam said a rise in the offering price would psychologically fuel more buying because "good things are always worth more".

Analysts expect the issue to be well received with a subscription of more than 600 times, which would make it one of the most popular issues ever. The grey market price of the stock was about HK$24 to HK$25, they said.

Beijing Enterprises holds stakes in brewer Yanjing Brewery, Beijing McDonald's and Western Food/Xinjing Food. It also has stakes in toll road operator Capital Expressway Co, Jianguo Hotel, the Wangfujing Group, and programmable switching systems maker Beijing International Switching System.
"People are not really buying such a high multiple company on the basis of the underlying current business, people are really buying expectation," Xue said.
Peregrine Capital Ltd and Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd will be the global co-ordinators and sponsors of the share issue.
